newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lasting heat spell could hit French maize -analyst.
newsitem.headline: Lasting heat spell could hit French maize -analyst.

text.p: French analyst Strategie Grains said on Monday that it had raised its estimate for the French 1997 maize yield to 8.2 tonnes per hectare from 8.1 forecast last month, due to good growing conditions until end-July. This would compare with 8.38 tonnes achieved in 1996.
But in its August report the analyst said that concern over the possible impact of a long heat wave in southern France limited the size of the revision.
To end-July, crop development was satisfactory throughout France and the yield potential "excellent" in the Poitou-Charentes, Midi-Pyrenees, Aquitaine and Alsace regions.
But substantial rain in May and June prevented maize roots from fully developing and reaching deep into the ground, making them more vulnerable to high temperatures and lasting dry conditions.
In fact temperatures were above 30 degrees Celsius in the southwest during the first week of August.
"If this situation persists, the potential of non-irrigated maize will be hit," the analyst said.
"In view of the number of kernels (per ear) and plant development up to now, the yield potential seems to be above or equal to 8.1 tonnes..."
"We are raising our forecast to 8.2 tonnes per hectare but no more for the moment due to high temperatures in early August in the south of France", it said.
Strategie Grains predicted a 1997 maize crop at 14.4 million tonnes, "with a possible range of 13.8 to 14.9 million tonnes" against 14.5 million tonnes in 1996.
